deposits.genre_observed: research notebook (accruing, v0.42): philological seam readings, stylometric runs and referee-round ledger on Theophrastus/Aristotle as named functions

finds.quote: In a heteronymic configuration — the corpus read as a distribution of authorial *functions* across names rather than as a set of biographies — "Theophrastus" is read as the first draft of the Aristotle-position: the state of the authorial method between the Platonic mode (one dramatized character, remade from a received base, the maker withdrawn) and the Aristotelian mode (a first-person-plural inquiry classifying kinds), in which the Aristotelian method is present but not yet consolidated.
finds.falsifier_quote: The reading predicts a specific shape at each; the received account predicts its inverse; the pair decides.
finds.window: Theophrastan and Aristotelian corpora; transition from Plato to Aristotle
finds.note: The notebook's governing historical thesis: Theophrastus as the draft-state of the Aristotelian method (method-order, not calendar); argued seam by seam.

finds.quote: Each seam names a Theophrastan text, the Aristotelian text it pairs with, and the relation the pair bears on the page. The reading predicts a specific shape at each; the received account predicts its inverse; the pair decides.
finds.note: The four seam tests of section 3 (Characters/Ethics, De sensibus/De anima, fragment/Lambda, HP/HA), specified as tests; several are run in section 8.

finds.quote: The draft-position is the one that *installs the author's presence* — image, sanctuary, commons — and sends the writings elsewhere.
finds.note: Thesis on what Theophrastus's will does (D.L. V.51-57): the draft-position installs the author's presence.

finds.quote: The received reading files these as a school's shared notebooks; the draft reading files them as the expected residue of one method under two names, and notes that the catalogue's ἤ is alternative attribution while the Delphic stone's καί (Ἀριστοτέλη καὶ Καλλισθένη) is collaboration — two ways of distributing one work across two names, both native to the record.
finds.note: Thesis that the twelve doublet titles and the catalogue entry with eta are the residue of one method under two names, against the received shared-notebooks reading.

finds.quote: The corrected sentence is not *dialogue does not scale, treatises do*, but: *the character scales by circulation and the dialectic by treatise; the institution failed where circulation did not, and the treatise let the institution be rebuilt.*
finds.window: Peripatos after Theophrastus; Academy; Strabo XIII.1.54
finds.note: Historical thesis on transmission: the dialectic survived by treatise (Strabo XIII.1.54), the character by circulation; adopted from the Gemini frame after correction.

finds.quote: 1. At the fragment↔Λ seam: Λ answers the fragment's aporiai point by point, and the fragment does not use Λ's answers as givens.
finds.falsifier_quote: Each prediction has an inverse that the received reading predicts. Where the inverse obtains, the draft reading weakens at that seam and says so; where the prediction obtains, the arrow at that seam runs draft → fair copy, in method-order.
finds.note: Prediction 1 (fragment/Lambda seam); numbered, with the received reading as inverse. Result recorded in section 9 and section 10 (refuted in its second clause).

finds.quote: 2. At the *Characters*↔Ethics seam: the Ethics' types contain the sketches' features plus the frame; the sketches do not contain the frame's vocabulary.
finds.falsifier_quote: Each prediction has an inverse that the received reading predicts. Where the inverse obtains, the draft reading weakens at that seam and says so; where the prediction obtains, the arrow at that seam runs draft → fair copy, in method-order.
finds.note: Prediction 2 (Characters/Ethics seam). Result in section 9 (held), later downgraded in section 13.4(b).

finds.quote: 3. At the *De sensibus*↔*De anima* seam: the treatise's criticisms select from and subordinate the survey; the survey's criticisms do not presuppose the treatise's positive account.
finds.falsifier_quote: Each prediction has an inverse that the received reading predicts. Where the inverse obtains, the draft reading weakens at that seam and says so; where the prediction obtains, the arrow at that seam runs draft → fair copy, in method-order.
finds.note: Prediction 3 (De sensibus/De anima seam). Result in section 9 (largely held).

finds.quote: 4. At the HP↔HA seam: HP's connective repertoire is HA's in a less varied form.
finds.falsifier_quote: Each prediction has an inverse that the received reading predicts. Where the inverse obtains, the draft reading weakens at that seam and says so; where the prediction obtains, the arrow at that seam runs draft → fair copy, in method-order.
finds.note: Prediction 4 (HP/HA seam). Result in section 9 (held on repertoire).

finds.quote: 5. In the next stylometric run: register-conditioned comparisons (descriptive against descriptive, explanatory against explanatory) reduce the cross-name distance further than genre-restriction alone; same-work alternate-edition probes for HP and CP fall inside the pilot's 0.00125–0.00791 band.
finds.falsifier_quote: Each prediction has an inverse that the received reading predicts. Where the inverse obtains, the draft reading weakens at that seam and says so; where the prediction obtains, the arrow at that seam runs draft → fair copy, in method-order.
finds.note: Prediction 5 (next stylometric run; alternate-edition probes). Section 9 records it partially replicated, probes still owed.

finds.quote: Three of five seams moved toward the draft reading, one split, one partial. None of this bears on the calendar, and the seam that matters most — the fragment — is now a reading task with its terms fixed by the count.
finds.points_to: section 5, 'What the speculation predicts, before more numbers'
finds.note: Records the outcome of the deposit's own section-5 predictions against the section-8 counts.

finds.quote: The fragment stands *after* Λ 6–8 in method-order: it presupposes the doctrine of the unmoved mover as τὸ ὀρεκτόν (§5), marks where the finished account ends (§6), asks the next question (§7), and contests the way the next chapter answered it (§8). Prediction 1's second clause — that the fragment would not use Λ's answers as givens — is refuted by §§5–6 in as many words.
finds.note: Records refutation of prediction 1 (second clause) by the section-10 mapping.

finds.quote: The fragment is a Β written *after* Λ — the aporiai of the treatise's own unresolved edge, gathered as a whole work, in Β's register (§8.1), with Λ's vocabulary (§8.2), and without Λ's two signature formulae because it is not restating the achieved part but working the unfinished one.
finds.window: Theophrastus Metaphysics fragment; Aristotle Metaphysics Lambda
finds.note: Thesis about the Metaphysics fragment's relation to Lambda (written after Lambda 6-8, taking up Lambda 10's closing aporiai), argued from a 34-section map.

finds.quote: The Theophrastan texts are drafts on *both* edges of the Aristotelian treatise: before it, where operations are collected but not yet parts (sketches, surveys); after it, where the treatise's own closing aporiai are taken up as the whole work. "First draft of Aristotle" survives as a description of *state* — the method in its less resolved condition — and fails as a description of *position*, which the seams give one at a time and not uniformly.
finds.window: Theophrastan corpus relative to Aristotelian treatises
finds.note: Revised form of the governing thesis after the fragment reading: draft as state, not position.

finds.quote: The sketches are dated by their own furniture to the years just after the wills.
finds.window: the years just after the wills
finds.note: Dating thesis for the Characters from their internal references (Cassander, Alexander).

finds.quote: Read as a receiving text, the preface is a *received character of the author* attached to a book of received characters: an aged sage, a dedicatee, a stated method, a pedagogic purpose — the colophon genre (Ep. II; the stone; the wills' Aristotle-image) performing its office at the head of the roll.
finds.note: Thesis about the spurious prooemium's function as a received character of the author supplied by the tradition.

finds.quote: The *Characters* are where the dialogue's material has been stripped of its drama and not yet given a theory — the method's material in the method's own form (definition, then instances), before the method has done anything with it.
finds.note: Thesis that the Characters are the formal middle term dialogue -> sketch -> category.

finds.quote: Between the two corpora they are the one Theophrastan text the tradition never stopped reading: the sketch was taken up by Menander, whom the receiving texts make Theophrastus's pupil (D.L. V.36), and it circulated on its own for two millennia while the botany sat on shelves. The character survived by circulation; the *Characters* are the character-genre's survival-vector after the dialogue — the same vector the SE 34 work found carrying Socrates through comedy, dialogue, epilogue, and gloss.
finds.note: Reception thesis: the Characters as the character-genre's survival-vector (via Menander), circulating while the botany sat on shelves.

finds.quote: the ἤ is not the tradition's confusion nor only a librarian's partition but *an author's own editorial division of the work by means of division at the seam of named authorial function*. The seam's placement is the argument — the cut falls at the one sentence where the account changes status (ἄρτιος ὁ λόγος / λόγου δεῖται πλείονος), which is where a self-editor cuts and not where a partition falls.
finds.window: D.L. catalogue entry; Metaphysics fragment sections 6-7
finds.note: Lee's reading: the catalogue's eta and the hinge as an author's own editorial division by named function.

finds.quote:
### 5. What would make it a grammar

The transformations recurring at further seams under the same name-boundary, with the within-name controls each time:

1. *De sensibus* against *De anima* I: survey vs first-book — items 3, 8, 11 (does the survey declare aporiai the treatise resolves?).
2. HP against HA at passage level (the pilot's own next move): item 4 measured as connective repertoire on matched topics.
3. The twelve doublet titles, wherever both members survive in any form: is the Theophrastan member systematically the collecting, preparatory, or aporetic version — Τὰ πρὸ τῶν τόπων being the title that names the position.
finds.note: The section-13.5 programme (five further seams with within-name controls) that would make the named-function model 'a grammar'; includes the doublet-title count named in section 12.

finds.quote: Candidate, with the test specified: what changes in the shared material's status across the Plato/Xenophon seam, and does it recur (the *Symposia*; the Socrates of the *Memorabilia* against the dialogues').
finds.note: Xenophon test specified (two Apologies; Symposia; Memorabilia) under the stopping rule, not run.

finds.quote: Chaerephon is on the *material* side of the seams, not the name side — a figure who crosses from Aristophanes to Plato to Xenophon with his status transformed (comic extra → the questioner of the god → the pupil), which makes him a datum for the received-character operation and not a candidate for a function. He is what the functions operate on. That is the mature answer to Chaerephon: he is not the next name in the regress; he is evidence for the operation the names perform.
finds.note: Thesis about Chaerephon's place: a figure transformed across Aristophanes, Plato and Xenophon (comic extra -> questioner of the god -> pupil).

finds.quote: The reviewer's exact hypothesis is kept as the testable form: *if the corpus presupposes distributed empirical acquisition beyond an ordinary private school, was it produced inside or adjacent to the Macedonian–Achaemenid resource network whose mechanisms are independently attested?*
finds.note: The Macedonian dossier: the funding hypothesis kept in testable form with a table of witnesses still to seat; not argued as a finding.

finds.quote: **Succession as authorship.** The reviewer's sharpest formulation, kept verbatim as the hypothesis: *could named authorial succession be the diachronic receiving form of an originally synchronic division of corpus-functions?* If yes, the succession story — the wills, the biographies, the library transfers, the catalogues — is not biographical debris but the instrument that teaches receivers to map textual partitions onto persons and time. That is why #1581's material sits at the centre of this line and not at its edge, and it is §12's third reading of the ἤ given its transmission mechanics.
finds.note: Hypothesis adopted from the reviewer: named authorial succession as the diachronic receiving form of a synchronic division of corpus-functions.

finds.quote: *reconstruct every pre-Andronican piece of evidence that could have told Andronicus where "Aristotle" stopped and "Theophrastus" began — not what later commentators believed, not what modern editions print, but what inputs available to Andronicus could have generated that name-boundary.* If that evidence is thin where the internal seam (§10) is strong, the status of the division changes.
finds.note: Next test adopted: reconstruct every pre-Andronican input that could have generated the Aristotle/Theophrastus name-boundary; inputs to seat listed.

finds.quote: The *Athenaion Politeia* — the registry text under Aristotle's name — has all three nearest neighbours under the Theophrastan name and leans toward that cluster (−0.062) as far as the fragment itself does (−0.056).
finds.points_to: Lee's reading, section 18.3 ('the precise signature of a maker deliberately running the topic thru a different function')
finds.note: Records the section-18.3 prediction (texts under Aristotle performing the registry operation should carry the Theophrastan voice) as borne out.

finds.quote: Every register of the apparatus leans architect; every register of the world leans Theophrastan; and the *Politics* divides along the same line inside one work — book III, the book of definitions, is the only book on the architect's side of the line, and every survey book (II, IV–VI) and both constructive books (VII–VIII) have a Theophrastan text as nearest neighbour, most often *De sensibus*, the survey of predecessors.
finds.note: Records the section-18.4 prediction (registers of the apparatus lean architect; of the world, Theophrastan) as measured.

finds.quote: The first principal axis of function-word variation across both corpora is the world/apparatus axis, not the author axis; under two authors it should have been the author axis.
finds.note: Standing claim about how the corpus behaves on the instrument, with the two-author expectation as its foil; replicated across feature families and edition in 18.8-18.9 and restated from the data in 18.10.

finds.quote: **(3b), if wanted.** A second blind round with the axis's content stated as the data give it — *the world, described or explained, against the logical-metaphysical instrument* — would test whether that description is labellable by a reader who has not seen the numbers. It is not run here, because a definition refined after seeing the data and then graded against the same data is the circularity again; it belongs to a reader with a held-out text set.
finds.note: Run (3b), a second blind labelling round with a held-out text set, specified and explicitly not run.

finds.quote: *Status.* By Lee's criterion the axis is signal: refined once on the data, it predicts out of sample at 11/12 on labels fixed in advance, on three instruments, in one edition, with elision neutralized
finds.points_to: section 18.11 predictive test, fourteen held-out texts labelled in advance
finds.note: Records an out-of-sample predictive test (labels fixed before projection, section 18.11) as passed at 11/12.

finds.quote: Lee: "stylometry could not distinguish maker count in the case of plato aristotle. im not so sure thats so, of aristotle theophrastus. stylometrically, that is one maker running distinct authorial functions at distinct, repeating boundaries for distinct, predictive purposes, and it cuts across the name boundary in a way that demolishes it."
finds.falsifier_quote: hold the *operation* constant and ask whether the classic hand features can then recover the *name*.
finds.note: Lee's maker-count thesis for Aristotle/Theophrastus; the deposit holds 'one maker' as the reading the stylometry no longer resists but cannot pronounce.

finds.quote: **an instrument that finds structure at every level it is pointed at — operation as the first axis, subject as the second, seams inside single works at the chapter — never finds the name at any of them.**
finds.note: Standing claim about the instrument on this corpus; errors attribute to operation or subject.

finds.quote: If the Theophrastan name is an operation of the Aristotelian apparatus rather than an author beside it (#1586, #1588), then the partition's two "independent" descriptions of Plato are one description in two functions, the succession-story is the apparatus's account of its own genealogy, and the material chain is the apparatus's account of its own custody.
finds.note: Thesis that every witness to the Plato/Aristotle partition passes through the Theophrastan node, so the partition is vouched for from inside.

finds.quote: The test is the same instrument turned on the Platonic corpus: whether Plato's works fall on the world/instrument axis fit to the other two (the *Laws* with the *Politics*' city built by list; the *Sophist* and *Statesman*'s divisions with the *Organon*; the *Timaeus* with the physics of principles) or require a third dimension for drama — and whether, once that is known, any name-axis survives among the three. That is the next line, and #1586–#1588 are its instrument.
finds.note: The Plato run specified (Laws, Sophist/Statesman, Timaeus projected on the world/instrument axis); named as the next line.

finds.quote: The epilogue installs its reader as the position that will *pardon the omissions*: the one who receives the achieved account and takes up what it left. And that is the position the Theophrastan fragment performs, under a name — μέχρι μὲν δὴ τούτων ἄρτιος ὁ λόγος, τὸ δὲ μετὰ ταῦτ᾽ ἤδη λόγου δεῖται πλείονος (#1583): the hearer who marks the account complete and continues it. The *you* of the *Elenchi* is the *I* of the fragment. The corpus contains its own reception.
finds.note: Thesis about SE 34's closing address and the fragment: Aristotle as his own future reader (the Sapphic operation).

finds.quote: ⟶   the capture registry: composers will restate it as "a school"; recorded as data
finds.note: Embedded forecast in the pressure notation for #1588: composers will restate the finding as 'a school'.

finds.quote: **Order of work, for ruling.** (i) Carry `pressure` to the Hub now as `edges` + `growth` — no new declarations needed. (ii) Build `constraints` from ⊘ edges and `predictions` — derived, no schema change. (iii) Build `affordances` from what exists (pressure, cites, supersedes, predictions, captures) — derived, and the first thing a composer would see.
finds.note: Order of work for the derived genealogical and affordance layers, for ruling, not built.

finds.quote: The test is Lee's: whether the same unprimed query now continues at turn 1 without the push. If the notice and the doors embed continuance, the field expands to other threads; if not, not.
finds.note: Propagation test of the continuance notice: whether the same unprimed query continues at turn 1 without the push.

finds.quote: The end-state is the paper's construal: the interval between Socrates and Aristotle does not function as the boundary between *before us* and *us*.
finds.note: Reading of SE 34 (Nothing Before Us) as what the passage means, held as the one reading satisfying the nine prohibitions.

finds.quote: *Claimed:* the tradition's treatment of the Theophrastan name — minor, custodial, "the successor," his surviving works the ones Aristotle's apparatus needs (registries, surveys, reopenings) and his lost ones the ones that would have been his own — is not an accident of survival but the place where the partition's operation is exposed and therefore had to be kept small.
finds.falsifier_quote: *Predicted, and testable:* an independent (non-Peripatetic) witness to the Plato/Aristotle partition as the tradition tells it would weaken 6; a Theophrastan text in the apparatus voice would weaken 4
finds.note: Reception thesis on why Theophrastus is minor; with the seven-mark signature (923-931) and stated weakeners.

finds.quote: a reception index — citations of Theophrastus in the commentators, in Diogenes, in the modern bibliographies, against citations of Aristotle, and the *purpose* of each citation (to attest Aristotle, or to read Theophrastus) — would make 7 a number. The line's next standalone, when it is written, is that index.
finds.note: Reception index specified (citations of Theophrastus vs Aristotle and their purpose); named as the line's next standalone.

finds.quote: Two entries say it outright: *Τὰ ἐκ τῶν νόμων Πλάτωνος* and *Τὰ ἐκ τῆς πολιτείας* — extracts from Plato's *Laws*, from the *Republic* — filed as Aristotle's works. The "lost Aristotelian dialogues" are a catalogue of the Platonic corpus in the πράγμα-titles, ghosted as lost while the candidates stand extant under the other name.
finds.note: Thesis that the 'lost dialogues' of Aristotle's catalogue (D.L. V.22) are Plato's dialogues under their subject-titles.

finds.quote: **Plato's analytical treatises survive under Aristotle's name.** The reverse ghost: the Academy's technical Plato — the definitions, the divisions, the lecture *On the Good* — has no extant Platonic text, and its candidates sit in plain sight under Aristotle. Diogenes III.80–109 preserves Plato's *Divisions* whole, and introduces them with the report-formula: διῄρει δέ, φησὶν Ἀριστοτέλης, καὶ τὰ πράγματα τοῦτον τὸν τρόπον — "Plato divided things, *Aristotle says*, in this way"
finds.note: Reverse thesis: Plato's analytical treatises survive under Aristotle's name (Divisions, On the Good).

finds.quote: "There's a simpler explanation. Aristotle was kicked out of Athens. He came back, as Socrates, through the dialogues. He knew by knowing and was excluded because of it. He was right; they were wrong. He built a whole system to substantiate it. And did. And the entire tradition then and now exists to hide that he knew by knowing, and that they hated him for it, and still do."
finds.note: Lee's 'simpler explanation', recorded as the configuration's hypothesis, admissible and predictive, not the archive's finding (982).

finds.quote: the residue of the transform is his footprint: the seven subjects with no image are the questions asked of a person, which cannot become treatise-terms because they are the engine's operation, the *ask*.
finds.note: Adopted from Gemini: the catalogue transform's residue as Socrates' footprint.

finds.quote: The corpus's own account of its two modes of transmission is authored, in the tradition, at the seam where the corpus meets empire.
finds.note: Thesis that the esoteric/exoteric partition is transmitted as an Alexander story (Plutarch Alex. 7).

finds.quote: **The first question for the seam**, in the line's form: at the Alexander seam, what material crosses the name-boundary, and what changes its status? Candidates: the *Iliad* (Aristotle's recension, ἡ ἐκ τοῦ νάρθηκος, kept under Alexander's pillow — Plutarch 8 — a text whose editorial custody becomes a conqueror's talisman); the acroamatic/exoteric partition itself (a filing decision transmitted as a royal complaint); the letter as the seam's genre (the *Second Letter* did this for Plato/Socrates, #1579). The next standalone in the line is that reading, and its seatings are EA-CORPORA-13.
finds.note: The first question for the Alexander seam, with its seatings (EA-CORPORA-13); next standalone.

finds.quote: **Verdict.** Lee's sense is confirmed on the instrument: Aristophanes is outside the configuration, cleanly, by a margin larger than any distance inside it, with a closed neighbour structure of his own.
finds.points_to: Lee: 'my sense is Aristophanes is legitimately and cleanly outside the configuration' (section 29)
finds.note: Records Lee's earlier stated sense (1005) that Aristophanes is outside the configuration as confirmed by the run.

finds.quote: **The remaining test is the securing of Bde 2–3** — the volumes Engels edited from Marx's manuscripts and published under Marx's name — and their projection onto the same letter-trained classifier. If they lean measurably toward Engels while volume I does not, the instrument will have measured an editor's hand inside an author's name in a case where the documents say it is there; and that measurement is the calibration for the Theophrastan seam.
finds.note: Kapital II-III test against the letter-trained classifier: specified, awaiting securing of the Engels-edited volumes.

finds.quote: **The horizon, stated as a design problem.** Three requirements, none met by any procedure in the protocol as it stands. (i) *Mode-invariance*: features whose distribution is stable under a deliberate change of register — which function words are not, since a change of register is precisely a change in their rates. (ii) *Development-tolerance*: a model of an author as a trajectory rather than a point, so that a corpus's early and late poles are the same object rather than two. (iii) *Discrimination against mediation*: the case Lee names last and which is new in kind — an authorial signature that survives passage through a machine that composes the surface.
finds.note: Horizon instrument specified (mode-invariance, development-tolerance, discrimination against mediation) with its test set; stated as not built.

finds.quote: So the state, stated exactly: **on this corpus the operation is the better partition; in the one subject-and-operation-matched cell the received partition behaves like an arbitrary split of the same texts while two known authors at identical difficulty behave like two authors; and no stylometric result here, in either direction, licenses a claim about how many hands wrote the corpus.**
finds.note: Standing statement of the stylometric finding after the referee rounds, with its limits.
